title: Narrow `release triage` to issues confirmed on the latest release
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #195152. That PR told the bot to apply `release triage` generously, on any of five criteria, and to add it when unsure. In practice that is too wide a net: severity alone ("crash", "silent correctness", "packaging") matches a large share of the incoming queue, and "would ship broken in the next release" is a judgement the bot cannot make from the issue text.

Replace the five criteria with two gates, either of which is sufficient:

1. The issue states a PyTorch version and it is the most recent released minor (from the `RELEASE CONTEXT` block) or one of its patches.
2. The issue already carries `high priority`, applied by a human.

Everything else is out, including main/nightly/RC-only reproductions and issues with no version stated. When the release version is `unknown` the label is not applied at all, rather than falling back to the severity criteria.

Also flips the tie-break: "when unsure, leave it off" instead of "when unsure, add it". The label is worked through by hand, so a list that fills with maybes stops being read. Genuinely urgent issues still reach a human via `triage review` in 5a, which is unchanged.

## Test plan

Documentation-only change to `.claude/skills/triaging-issues/SKILL.md` (+39/-35, one file). No code paths affected; the skill text is read by the triage bot at invocation time.

cc @pytorch/pytorch-dev-infra

Done with assitance of Claude
